service: Hyper3D Rodin (hyper3d.ai), Business plan, through the hyper3d MCP server
prompt: An old rotary desk telephone in charcoal black with a big cream dial with round finger holes, its chunky handset knocked crooked on the cradle, one end tilted up. No cord. Hand-sculpted matte modeling clay, stop-motion claymation style, chunky rounded forms. One single closed object, no base, no text, no logos.

files.model.fbx: Rodin's base_basic_pbr.fbx; its embedded diffuse map is the final one, and its normal, roughness and metallic maps are flat 1-pixel images (flat normal, roughness 0.85, not metallic), so the clay stays matte

credits: Rodin reports no cost per call; about 0.5 credit a generation (T81's measurement). T105's total is in Docs/tasks/T105.md.
note: The curly cord stayed in both takes (the image wins over the prompt). Take 2 is kept: one closed piece, where take 1's cord was 19 loose pieces. My person chose to keep the cord.
